items.caption: This instance listens to the traffic of all Comet WiFi thermostats and collects which devices report in. From the list below you can create an instance for each device.

⏳  Devices only appear once they send something on their own — this can take minutes to hours. The configurator deliberately queries nothing, to spare the batteries. If you do not want to wait, briefly cut the power to the thermostat in question (take the battery out and put it back in); it reports in immediately afterwards.
Matching to instances that already exist is done via the MAC address, not the name. Renamed instances are therefore still recognised correctly.
This instance must be placed under an MQTT Client (or MQTT Server) that is connected to the thermostats' broker.

items.name: MQTTUser
items.caption: MQTT user
What is the MQTT user?
The eight-character account identifier shared by all Comet WiFi devices of one account. It is different for every user — there is no sensible default.
It can be read from a device's MQTT connection setup (port 1883 is unencrypted), see the README.

The thermostats normally get their time from the manufacturer's cloud. Without it the clocks drift and the weekly schedule runs at the wrong time.

⚠️  This function affects ALL Comet WiFi devices on the network, not only the ones created here — the time channel is a broadcast. Only switch it on if the connection to the manufacturer's cloud is permanently gone.

items.name: TimeSyncHours
items.caption: Every … hours

After a module update, Symcon does not always apply an instance's settings by itself. The only other way is to change something in the form and change it back — only then does "Apply" become clickable at all. This button saves you that.
⚠️  Acts on the saved settings. Anything you changed above but have not applied yet is lost.
This is harmless for the devices: applying sends nothing and therefore does not wake any battery.
🔄  Force apply (without a form change)

items.caption: This configurator only listens and sends nothing at all — that is why there is deliberately no "Search for devices now" button: every query would wake a battery-powered device.
"Last" in the line above is therefore the time of the last device message, not of a search.

Every device whose messages match the configured MQTT user and topic prefix is detected. Matching to instances that already exist works via the MAC address and the shared broker — explicitly not via the name.
Entries disappear again when a device has not reported for longer than the configured time.
